glyph_origin: The oracle-bone forms of 西 fall into two types: open-topped and closed-topped. The open-topped type is found only in periods I–II, especially in the Bin and Chu groups; later scripts inherit the closed-topped type. The open-topped form has been interpreted as a bird's nest, possibly related to 栖 (“to perch; to roost”). The later closed-topped form may be related to 囟: in the Zhouyuan oracle-bone inscriptions, 囟 is used for 西.
senses: [xī] (Cantonese, minced oath) euphemistic form of 閪
to spin; to cause to spin
